title: I'm building a WW2 squad stealth game. What's your first impression?
author: rpostulart
selftext:
I'm a solo dev building an isometric WW2 squad stealth game, in the spirit of the old tactics games. You lead three specialists through occupied coastal villages at night: a knife, a rifle, and wire cutters with tin-can decoys. No mission can be won without every character you bring, and they have to cooperate.

I'm not asking about gameplay yet. I want to know what you think and feel when you first see it:

1. In one sentence, what kind of game do you think this is?
2. Does the style make you want to play it, and why or why not?
3. Is it clear which characters or things on screen matter?
4. Anything that looks off, confusing, or generic?

Blunt answers are welcome. Screenshots are from five different levels, all real gameplay.

Art note: the art is AI-assisted and fixed by hand, the code is built with AI coding tools. I'd rather say that up front.

replies.author: Free-Schedule1948

replies.author: rpostulart

comments.author: COLDCRUSHCASM
comments.body:
This is really nice. One of the better/best AI games I have seen in a while. It gives me alot of great old-school commandos vibes. The only feedback I would give you is on some of the UI, It feels very clean and nice and doesnt scream the usual obvious Claude AI style but there might be some light theming you can do on some more elements. The icons are solid  but your character faces are a little out of place looking with the realism. I would pick some characters in a cool modern animated show you like the look of and train off that. Heres a tip. get your reference style and character set, then ask chat gpt something like  
  
''Create a 3D high-end character portrait of the reference as if rendered by a zbrush artist for a stylized AAA game. Render it as a sculpt with no color texture, but with normal, specular, metal, etc with three point lighting with a rim light on the right side. Angular features, in the style of a 1950's comic book. On a flat gray background. ''  


That's the first step, then ask your llm to give you a breakdown of your texture reference and then ask it to apply that style to the faces. 

This should get you a decent look that feels more in keeping with the style of your game, and a little more fun. You can also try this with items / guns as well with a few changes

Overall just want to commend you on this game, looks really good man, would love to know a little more about your workflow
